children.title: Trump removes NSA and Cyber Command chief Timothy Haugh
children.description_medium: On April 4, 2025, Trump dismissed Gen. Timothy Haugh as director of the NSA and head of U.S. Cyber Command, and deputy Wendy Noble was reassigned. The removals followed a White House meeting with Laura Loomer, who had urged Trump to remove officials she considered disloyal and had criticized Haugh. Trump and administration officials made the personnel decisions.
children.description_long: President Donald Trump dismissed Gen. Timothy Haugh as director of the National Security Agency and head of U.S. Cyber Command on April 4, 2025; Haugh’s deputy, Wendy Noble, was reassigned. Reuters reported that the removals followed a White House meeting with activist Laura Loomer. Loomer had urged Trump to remove officials she viewed as disloyal and had criticized Haugh. The supplied reporting supports the personnel actions and the context of Loomer’s advocacy, while identifying Trump and administration officials as the decision-makers. It does not support describing Loomer as having issued an order or formally made the removals. This April personnel episode is distinct from Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard’s August announcement revoking 37 current and former intelligence officials’ security clearances. The sources describe the leadership change at NSA and Cyber Command, as well as Noble’s reassignment; they do not establish the later duration of the leadership vacancy or that the action was part of a single operation directed by Loomer. The personnel changes should be dated to April 4 and attributed to the administration.
children.date_uncertainty: The date is the reported personnel-action date; Reuters published its coverage on April 4, 2025.

children.title: Gabbard revokes 37 intelligence officials’ security clearances
children.description_medium: On August 19, 2025, Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard revoked the security clearances of 37 current and former intelligence professionals. She said Trump directed the action and accused the individuals of politicizing intelligence; the supplied reporting does not connect the decision to Laura Loomer.
children.description_long: Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard revoked the security clearances of 37 current and former intelligence professionals, Reuters reported on August 19, 2025. Gabbard said Trump had directed the action and accused the individuals of politicizing intelligence. The supplied account describes a clearance decision announced by Gabbard and attributed by her to presidential direction. It does not connect the August action to Laura Loomer, who had advocated for removals during a separate April episode that included the dismissal of NSA and Cyber Command chief Timothy Haugh. The two actions should therefore remain separate in the record. The available evidence supports the number of people affected, Gabbard’s stated attribution and accusation, and the date of the public announcement; it does not establish that Loomer caused or ordered this clearance revocation. The announcement concerned current and former members of the intelligence community and involved removal of clearances, a distinct personnel measure from Haugh’s dismissal and Noble’s reassignment. The cited reporting does not identify these actions as one combined purge.
children.date_uncertainty: The date is the Reuters publication and reported announcement date; the source does not separately date the underlying clearance processing.

unresolved_components.title: Loomer’s alleged role in August clearance revocations
unresolved_components.reason: The packet finds no accepted source linking Loomer to that action and says 'on Loomer's orders' overstates her role.
unresolved_components.missing_evidence: Direct reporting or documentation connecting Loomer’s actions to the August 37-clearance decision.

rationale: The packet supports two separate personnel actions with different dates and decision chains. The descriptions attribute Loomer’s advocacy and Gabbard’s stated direction without claiming unsupported causality.
